key_insight: Deep generative crystal structure prediction currently behaves more like a softened prototype-retrieval system than a truly de novo structure generator.
engineering_relevance: For CSP workflows, the practical value of generative models depends on improving retrieval-independent generalization, not just overall top-1 accuracy.
method: Benchmarked 12 generative CSP architectures across latent-variable, diffusion, flow-matching, autoregressive, and manifold random-walk families.
Compared them against TCSP 2.0 using identical structure-matching, symmetry, and consensus criteria.
Ran a leakage-controlled retraining test by removing entire stoichiometric prototype families from training data.
evidence_signal: On 180 test structures, template retrieval achieved 68.3% top-1 success, while the best generative models reached 66.4% and 62.9%; performance dropped 50–78% after prototype-family removal in four controlled retraining tests.
watch_item: High aggregate accuracy can mask strong dependence on known prototype families, so deployment claims should account for data leakage and prototype overlap.
paper_title: Deep Generative Crystal Structure Prediction: A Benchmark Study and a Controlled Test of Prototype Dependence
